hints: Look closely at the four column headings and ask yourself what must line the inside of every blood vessel to give smooth blood flow.
Remember arteries carry blood at very high pressure from the heart, so think which tissues allow stretch and recoil, controlled narrowing, and strength to prevent bursting.
walkthrough:
**Picture the artery wall**

Think of an artery in cross section. You already know it has a tunica intima, a tunica media and a tunica externa. Each layer contributes a different tissue.

All blood vessels are lined by endothelium, so that must be present.

**Match each tissue to its job**

Endothelium gives a smooth, non-sticky lining to reduce friction. Smooth muscle in the middle layer allows vasoconstriction to control blood flow. Elastic tissue allows the wall to stretch when the heart pumps and recoil to maintain pressure. Collagen fibres in the outer layer give great tensile strength to stop the wall tearing.

**Pick the matching row**

Since an artery needs all four jobs, lining, contraction, elasticity and strength, all four tissues must be present. That is only row A.

options.A: Correct. Arteries contain endothelium for smooth lining, smooth muscle for vasoconstriction, elastic tissue for stretch and recoil, and collagen for strength.
options.B: Not correct. Collagen fibres are present in the outer tunica externa to provide tensile strength and prevent over-stretching.
options.C: Not correct. Smooth muscle is present in the tunica media and is essential for vasoconstriction and control of blood distribution.
options.D: Not correct. Endothelium lines all arteries and elastic tissue is abundant in the wall to smooth out pressure pulses.
